newsitem.title: TAIWAN: ATHLETICS-CHINA ATHLETES POSTPONE TAIWAN VISIT ON DENG DEATH.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-CHINA ATHLETES POSTPONE TAIWAN VISIT ON DENG DEATH.

text.p: Twelve Atlanta Olympic gold medallists from China have postponed a scheduled visit to Taiwan after news that China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping had died, state television reported on Thursday.
"The visit has been postponed indefinitely because of the death of Deng Xiaoping," the television said.

The Chinese delegation, which included women's 5,000 metres gold medallist Wang Junxia and eight coaches, had been scheduled to arrive on Thursday at the invitation of Taiwan's education ministry to help promote bilateral sport exchanges.
Men's gymnastics all-round winner Li Xiaoshuang and women's diving gold medallist Fu Mingxia were also in the delegation.
China's paramount leader died late on Wednesday from respiratory failure. He was 92.
Although Taiwan and China have been political rivals since they split after a civil war ended in 1949, cultural and economic ties have flourished with an unofficial thaw that began in the 1980s.
